data.name: Rolfe
data.gender_notes: Rolfe is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old High German words hrod, meaning 'fame,' and wulf, meaning 'wolf.' The name Rolfe can be interpreted as 'counselor with famous wolf.'. The name Rolfe carries the meaning “Wolf counselor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rolfe usually hope their child will grow to embody wolf counselor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Rolfe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wolf counselor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rolfe total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_english.name: Rolfe
in_english.long_meaning: Adviser with the strength of a wolf

data.cultural_impact: The name Rolfe gained popularity in the English-speaking world due to the influence of Anglo-Saxon literature, particularly through characters in the epic poem Beowulf and other Old English sources. It signified strength, courage, and wise counsel, making it a coveted name for warriors and leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Rolfs' roots in Old High German (and meaning 'counselor with famous wolf') can represent both a protective guardian spirit as well as a wise and trusted spiritual advisor. It can serve as a reminder to seek the strength and guidance of both human counsel and Divine Providence.
